anomalies.observed: U9 pin 2 (EN) is not connected to any net; the netlist marks it as unconnected-(U9-EN-Pad2).
anomalies.expected: The TPS62933 enable pin must be tied to VIN or a pull-up to enable the 24V-to-5V buck regulator.
anomalies.impact: The 5V rail may not start up, disabling the ESP32 and all downstream 3.3V logic.

anomalies.observed: U6 pins 9 and 10 (MS1/AD0, MS2/AD1) and U7 pin 9 (MS1/AD0) are left floating; only U3 has both MS pins tied to +3V3, and U7 pin 10 is tied to +3V3.
anomalies.expected: MS1/AD0 and MS2/AD1 must be tied to GND or VCC_IO to set a defined UART address and microstep resolution for each TMC2209.
anomalies.impact: UART communication with U6 and U7 will fail due to undefined addresses, and microstep resolution will be undefined, potentially causing incorrect motor operation.

anomalies.observed: T2 is a P-channel MOSFET (AON6407) with source (pin 2) on /+24V_F (input after fuse) and drain (pin 3) on +24V (bulk rail).
anomalies.expected: For reverse polarity protection, the P-channel MOSFET should have its source on the load side (+24V) and drain on the input side (/+24V_F) so the body diode blocks reverse current.
anomalies.impact: Reverse polarity protection is defeated; a reversed 24V input will forward-bias the body diode and apply reverse voltage to the board, potentially damaging components.

These would prevent the 5V rail from starting, break UART/microstep configuration for two stepper drivers, and defeat reverse polarity protection.
